name: AutoAttack (Linf, standard)
tagline: Parameter-free ensemble of APGD-CE, APGD-DLR, FAB and Square Attack; the standard robustness-evaluation suite for $L_\infty$ adversaries.
pseudocode:
1. Use torchattacks.AutoAttack with norm='Linf', eps=eps, version='standard'.
2. Internally runs: APGD-CE -> APGD-DLR (targeted) -> FAB (targeted) -> Square Attack.
3. Each sub-attack is parameter-free and stops after step-size schedule converges.
4. Return adversarial images.
diff_from_baseline: Croce & Hein, 'Reliable Evaluation of Adversarial Robustness with an Ensemble of Diverse Parameter-free Attacks' (ICML 2020). The de-facto whitebox-attack benchmark.

name: FGSM (Fast Gradient Sign)
tagline: Single-step Linf attack: take the sign of the loss gradient and step by $\varepsilon$, clip to $[0,1]$.
diff_from_baseline: Goodfellow, Shlens & Szegedy, 'Explaining and Harnessing Adversarial Examples' (ICLR 2015). Original single-step adversarial attack; weakest baseline.

name: MI-FGSM (Momentum Iterative)
tagline: Iterative FGSM with a momentum-accumulated normalized gradient, improving transferability and stability over PGD.
pseudocode:
1. Init $x_0 = x + \mathrm{Uniform}(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$, clip to $[0,1]$; momentum $g_0=0$.
2. For 40 steps: compute $\nabla \mathrm{CE}$, normalize by per-image mean abs, accumulate $g \leftarrow \mu g + \hat\nabla$.
3. Step $x \leftarrow x + \alpha\,\mathrm{sign}(g)$ with $\alpha=\varepsilon/10$.
4. Project back to $L_\infty(\varepsilon)$ ball and clip to $[0,1]$.
diff_from_baseline: Dong et al., 'Boosting Adversarial Attacks with Momentum' (CVPR 2018). Adds Polyak momentum on per-image normalized gradients.

name: PGD (Projected Gradient Descent)
tagline: Iterative FGSM with random start: take signed gradient steps and project back to the $L_\infty(\varepsilon)$ ball after each step.
pseudocode:
1. $x_0 = x + \mathrm{Uniform}(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$, clip to $[0,1]$.
2. For 40 steps:
3.   $\nabla = \nabla_x \mathrm{CE}(f(x_t), y)$.
4.   $x_{t+1} = x_t + \alpha\,\mathrm{sign}(\nabla)$ with $\alpha=\varepsilon/4$.
5.   Project: clamp $x_{t+1}-x$ to $[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]$, then clip to $[0,1]$.
diff_from_baseline: Madry et al., 'Towards Deep Learning Models Resistant to Adversarial Attacks' (ICLR 2018). Canonical iterative whitebox $L_\infty$ attack.
